item.headline: Uber jumps 7% on higher-than-expected bookings guidance; consumer spending resilience confirmed
causal_chain: Uber Q1 earnings beat with forward bookings guidance above consensus, confirmed by Disney's parallel commentary on theme park and vacation spending resilience
Two independent data points from different consumer discretionary verticals (mobility/delivery and leisure) corroborate that the consumer spending backdrop remains robust despite macro uncertainty

Positive consumer health signal reduces credit-stress tail risk for travel and leisure names; UAL and NCLH held positions benefit from the same demand regime being re-confirmed ahead of their own catalysts
item.directional_bias: bullish consumer discretionary and travel/leisure; macro soft-landing narrative reinforced

sizing_recommendation.rationale: Consumer resilience confirmed across two independent verticals but signal is thematic/contextual rather than a direct UAL or NCLH catalyst; supports holding existing positions into their own catalysts without adding new risk

item.reasoning: The Uber guidance beat and Disney leisure commentary are the primary event and its sectoral echo — merged under the auto-merge rule (same macro theme, same-direction read from the same reporting cycle). For the portfolio, UAL is held into a binary earnings event and this data point is modestly supportive of the demand picture mapped in its thesis (support $88-92, binary catalyst). NCLH benefits similarly as cruise demand is part of the same consumer-leisure regime. Neither position should be sized up on this data alone — both have their own upcoming catalysts that will be the real signal — but the risk of a demand-side negative surprise is incrementally lower.

item.headline: Berkshire-owned McLane deploys Aurora autonomous big rigs across U.S. Sun Belt
causal_chain: Berkshire subsidiary McLane (major US distribution operator) commercially deploys Aurora autonomous trucks on live freight routes — this is a revenue-generating go-live, not a pilot announcement
Commercial validation from a Berkshire-grade counterparty materially de-risks Aurora's business model and reduces time-to-scale uncertainty for autonomous freight
Traditional long-haul trucking labor models face medium-term disruption signal; Aurora's competitive moat is strengthened relative to rivals still in testing phases
item.directional_bias: bullish Aurora and autonomous freight; neutral to mildly bearish traditional trucking operators over medium term

sizing_recommendation.rationale: Clean commercial milestone with a credible counterparty; no portfolio names directly affected; signal is sector-thematic rather than a held-position catalyst

item.reasoning: A Berkshire-quality operational deployment is a meaningful signal distinguishing Aurora from earlier-stage autonomous trucking ventures that collapsed (e.g., Convoy, TuSimple). The causal chain is clean but the broader market impact is medium-term and sector-specific. No current portfolio positions are affected. Worth flagging for anyone building a position in AUR or monitoring the autonomous logistics theme, but does not trigger portfolio action.

item.headline: Restaurant Brands International earnings top estimates, fueled by Burger King turnaround
causal_chain: QSR beats on revenue and EPS driven by Burger King same-store sales improvement, indicating the turnaround strategy is gaining traction
Positive QSR read-through suggests quick-service restaurant consumers remain value-seeking but still spending — partially consistent with the consumer resilience signal from the Uber/Disney item
Peers MCD and YUM face mild positive rerating on the same-store-sales read but QSR-specific operational execution is the primary driver, limiting direct comp implications
item.directional_bias: mildly bullish QSR; neutral read-through for broader QSR sector

sizing_recommendation.rationale: No portfolio exposure to QSR or direct peers; thematic signal is already captured in the Uber/Disney consumer resilience item; standalone actionability is low

item.reasoning: QSR beat is a company-specific positive that adds a third data point to the consumer-resilience theme building in this batch (alongside Uber and Disney). It modestly reinforces the soft-landing narrative but does not independently move the needle for any held portfolio position. Confidence is capped at 0.42 per low_specificity flag — the causal chain, while valid, has weak portfolio relevance.
